title: Use motifs to create contrast and interest

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines
location.section: Use motifs to create contrast and interest

slide_intent: Use a motif for a communication job because a recognizable shape can divide, connect or guide rather than merely decorate.
strategic_value: Selective wave use can make Helsinki layouts distinctive while leaving other identity elements room to work.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section explains functional wave roles, shows applied examples and follows them with guidance that motifs are optional.
practical_value: Decide what the wave should organize before including one, and omit it when color, imagery and type already carry the composition.

content_islands.name: Functional rationale
content_islands.spec: Explain contrast, cohesion, division and guidance.

content_islands.name: Applications with and without waves
content_islands.spec: Show a wave-divided photograph, plain blue flag and a montage of signage, print and annual covers.

content_islands.name: Restraint
content_islands.spec: End with text explaining why motifs are optional and should not be overused.

ingredient.name: Wave motif
ingredient.role: Organize and distinguish surfaces through a recognizable divider.
ingredient.application: Choose a motif that strengthens the message, using one motif per view; omit it when unnecessary.
ingredient.scope: One motif per view concerns motif choice, not an invented limit on the number of repeated wave tips.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explicitly gives waves functional roles of cohesion, division and guidance.
reference_purposes.Application: The examples place wave divisions in actual compositions.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Use only one motif per view; applications do not always require one.
